The opening of this collection moves through several tales: In “Kukkaislempeä,” Lauri Turkka, a fanatical botany docent repelled by human sexuality, reels from a friend’s engagement, spirals into delirium, and commits a sudden act of violence before begging to be taken to a hospital. “Pojan kissa” recalls a rainy‑night impulse to kick a trusting cat, then the shaming encounter with a fragile boy tenderly carrying the injured animal, which lodges in the narrator’s conscience. “Iloinen yllätys” is a taut dialogue in which Risto learns he likely has terminal cancer, debates the meaning of a “worthy” death with his physician friend Jussi, refuses surgery, and contemplates bequests as his only concrete gesture.
